sn41.1:1.1: Macchikāsaṇḍa was a township in Kāsī ([pli-tv-kd11:18.1.3]()), known only through its connection with Citta. The name probably means “Fisher’s Forest”.
sn41.1:2.1: The householder Citta, often identified as “of Macchikāsaṇḍa”,  was a chief lay disciple ([an2.132:1.2]()), foremost in teaching Dhamma ([an1.250]()). His boldness and intelligence mark his distinctive personality. | Migapathaka (“place of the animal track”) is only mentioned here.
sn41.1:2.2: The use of _kira_ here shows that he did not hear them directly, but heard a report. Hence below he says “I heard that …” (_sutaṁ metaṁ_), similar to the phrase “so I have heard” ([mn127:17.4]()).
sn41.1:4.6: This example is not attributed to the Buddha in the canon, so the question arises where Citta heard it. It is found in a discussion between Mahākoṭṭhita and Sāriputta ([sn35.232:4.3]()), but perhaps more relevant, between Kāmabhū and Ānanda ([sn35.233:4.3]()).
